industry: Small foodservice: cafes, coffee shops, restaurants

primary_sources.facts: Enerhodar cafe sole proprietor inspected; kitchen food waste, fryer and used vegetable oils reported; after prosecutor intervention waste passports developed and approved
Article 14 of 89-FZ and 2026 Order 286 passporting for classes I-IV

legal_basis.application: passporting only for wastes of hazard classes I-IV, classify each waste separately
current passporting procedure; not retroactive to June case

physical_chain: Cafe kitchen and food preparation -> food scraps, used fryer oil and other streams -> separate classification -> actual accumulation and transfer -> passports only where class I-IV applies
verified_evidence: Official prosecutor news dated 2026-06-15 documents completed remediation after inspection
limits: No proof the user's cafe was inspected; not all listed waste streams automatically require passports; exact codes/classes, inspection documents and sanctions for this case not established
risk: Small foodservice businesses may have unclassified I-IV waste streams despite considering themselves only TKO generators
red_flag: The business has a TKO collection contract but has not inventoried used cooking oil and other separately generated wastes
diagnostic_questions: Which distinct wastes arise from cooking, fryer use, maintenance and cleaning, and what are their verified FKKO codes and classes?
Does the actual accumulation and handover of each stream match the contracts and passport inventory?
Was the documentation requested by a regulator, landlord, contractor or initiated voluntarily?
mirlex_checks: separation of TKO and non-TKO streams
site: Waste card: add small foodservice as example only after source-verified classification
assistant: Ask process-first diagnostic questions; do not assume every cafe waste needs a passport

hypotheses.question: Are salons, cafes, bakeries and small food shops receiving more passport requests because of inspections, landlord audits or contractors?
